definitions.explanation: The native Japanese counter for nine objects.

examples.japanese: みかんを{九|ここの}つ{買|か}った。
{箱|はこ}の{中|なか}に{九|ここの}つあります。
examples.english: There are nine in the box.

examples.japanese: {質問|しつもん}が{九|ここの}つあります。
りんごを{九|ここの}つもらったので、{友達|ともだち}にも{分|わ}けた。
examples.english: I received nine apples, so I shared some with my friend.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{九|ここの}つのグループに{分|わ}かれて、それぞれ{違|ちが}う{歌|うた}を{練習|れんしゅう}した。
examples.english: The children divided into nine groups and each practiced a different song.

notes:
{九|ここの}つ is the native Japanese ({和語|わご}) number nine, used as a general counter for objects. This counting system only goes up to ten and is used when no specific counter applies.

NATIVE COUNTING SYSTEM ({和語|わご}):
- {一|ひと}つ (1), {二|ふた}つ (2), {三|みっ}つ (3), {四|よっ}つ (4), {五|いつ}つ (5)
- {六|むっ}つ (6), {七|なな}つ (7), {八|やっ}つ (8), {九|ここの}つ (9), {十|とお} (10)

WHEN TO USE:
- General objects without specific counters
- Abstract things: {理由|りゆう}が{九|ここの}つある (there are nine reasons)
- Food items at restaurants: りんごを{九|ここの}つ (nine apples)
- Age for children: {九|ここの}つ (nine years old, informal)

COMPARISON WITH SINO-JAPANESE:
- {九|ここの}つ: native counter (general objects)
- {九|きゅう}/{九|く}: Sino-Japanese reading (used with specific counters like {九人|きゅうにん}, {九個|きゅうこ})

NOTE: For numbers above ten, use Sino-Japanese numbers with appropriate counters.
